# GTNH Speedrun LiveSplit

Splits LiveSplit on milestones that the [GTNH Speedrun Audit](../gtnh-speedrun-audit) mod logs. The server has a
catalog of named milestones. Each runner picks which milestones are the segments of the runner's LiveSplit file. The
timer starts when the audit starts timing. Each split happens when its milestone is first reached, with LiveSplit's
game time set to the in-game time (IGT) of that moment.

A runner who joins a run in progress gets the run so far: their timer starts and splits each milestone already
reached, at the IGT of the milestone's first reach.

## Install

- Server: this mod and the audit mod.
- Each runner's client: this mod. Clients without it can still join.
- Singleplayer: both mods.

The server and the clients need the same version of this mod. The server logs `hello.rejected` for a client of
another version, and that client's timer doesn't split. The audit mod needs a version with the history API
(`AuditEvents.subscribeWithHistory`).

Pick your route first (see [Your route](#your-route)), then join the server and type `/livesplit export` in chat. The

## Timer setup

Pick your route first (see [Your route](#your-route)), then join the server and type `/livesplit export` in chat. The
mod writes `.minecraft/livesplit/<category>.lss` with a segment for each entry of your route, with the entry's name and
icon. Click the file name in chat to open the folder. Open the file in desktop LiveSplit (Open Splits) or LiveSplit
One (Splits, Import) once, before the first run. The file has no times, and the first run becomes the Personal Best.
An export never replaces a file: a second export of `Moon%` writes `Moon% (2).lss`.

Each icon is drawn once on export, the way an item in an inventory slot is drawn. Without Video Settings,
Enable FBOs, the file has no icons.

Desktop LiveSplit:

1. Right-click LiveSplit, then Control, then Start TCP/WS Server. To start the server with LiveSplit, set Startup
   Behavior in the settings.
2. Compare against Game Time.

LiveSplit One:

1. Start Minecraft. The mod listens on `ws://localhost:16835` from the main menu on.
2. Settings, Server Connection, Connect, then `ws://localhost:16835`.

2. Compare against Game Time.

LiveSplit One:

1. Start Minecraft. The mod listens on `ws://localhost:16835` from the main menu on.
2. Settings, Server Connection, Connect, then `ws://localhost:16835`.
3. Compare against Game Time.

LiveSplit One doesn't reconnect by itself. After a Minecraft restart, connect again.

Only the pages in `lsoAllowedOrigins` can connect to the port (see [Config](#config)). A connection from a browser
has the page's address in the `Origin` header, and a connection from another page gets 403. Add the address of a
LiveSplit One copy that you serve yourself.

A browser can block the public LiveSplit One page from connecting to `localhost`. Chrome asks for Local Network Access
("Apps on device" in newer versions). Allow it for one.livesplit.org.

## Joining a run in progress

When a runner joins, the runner's client gets the catalog, then every milestone reached so far, in the order reached,
then the current IGT. The client turns them into splits of the runner's route. A runner who rejoins gets the same
list, and no segment splits twice.

The server rebuilds the list from the audit log on each start, so a server restart loses nothing. LiveSplit's Game
Time of a caught-up split is the IGT of the milestone. The split's Real Time is the moment of the catch-up.

## Joining a run in progress

When a runner joins, the runner's client gets the catalog, then every milestone reached so far, in the order reached,
then the current IGT. The client turns them into splits of the runner's route. A runner who rejoins gets the same
list, and no segment splits twice.

The server rebuilds the list from the audit log on each start, so a server restart loses nothing. LiveSplit's Game
Time of a caught-up split is the IGT of the milestone. The split's Real Time is the moment of the catch-up.

After a rollback (a backup restore, or a crash before the world was saved), the milestones that the world lost are
gone from the list. On rejoin, the timer is unsplit back to the milestones the world still has. The timer splits a
lost milestone again when the run reaches the milestone again, at the new IGT. The lost lines stay in the audit log.

The server is the authority. While the run is going, the client checks the timer about once a second, and a split made
by hand past the server's list is undone.

context:
{"id": "nether", "name": "-Nether", "icon": "minecraft:obsidian@0"},
  {"name": "Steel + Tin", "allOf": ["steel", "tin"]},
  {"name": "Any Rubber", "anyOf": ["rubber_tree", "rubber_sapling"]}
]}
```

- A milestone id: the segment takes the milestone's name and icon.
- `{"id": …}` with a `name` or an `icon` for the segment. A name that starts with `-` is a subsplit in LiveSplit.
- `allOf`: for milestones a run can reach in any order. The segment splits when the last of them is reached, at that
  milestone's IGT.
- `anyOf`: the segment splits at the first of them.

LiveSplit splits its segments in a fixed order. When a later segment is reached first, `skipMissedSplits` decides what
happens (see [Config](#config)). Group milestones that come in any order with `allOf`.

The client reads the file on each join. A segment with a milestone id that the server doesn't have is left out, and chat
lists the ids. A file that can't be read is an empty route, and chat says why. Export the LiveSplit file again after you
change your route.

Commands:

- `/livesplit milestones [page]`: the server's milestones, with ids and the IGT of each one reached.
- `/livesplit route [page]`: your segments, with the IGT of each one reached, or how many milestones of a group are
  reached.
- `/livesplit export`: write the LiveSplit file of your route.

text: Press **Use held block** with an empty hand to carve.
context:
`/sclayers 10:stone *:grass 10:bedrock -s 3`. Each count is the thickness of a layer in
  blocks, from the highest block down. After the `*` layer, the counts are from the lowest
  block up, and the `*` layer fills the blocks between. Air stays air. `-s N` moves each band
  edge up or down by up to N blocks, in waves. N is from 0 to 32. The fill goes through your
  WorldEdit session, so `//gmask` and the block limit apply, and `//undo` reverts the fill.
  `/scu` does not revert the fill.
- **The panel has a Layers tab for the same fill.** Set up to 5 rows of a block and a count,
  mark one row as Rest, set the height variation, and press **Fill the WorldEdit selection**.
  The rows go to the server as a `/sclayers` command. Press the up arrow in chat to see the
  command again. A chat message has a limit of 100 characters, and 5 rows always fit.
- **"Replace only this block" has a separate block.** In 0.4.0, the mode compared each block
  with the brush material, so a sphere wrote stone over stone and changed nothing. Now a
  second block row is under the mode button. The brush writes the material only where the
  world has that block, with the same data value. Removal is checked too, so an air brush
  with dirt as the replace block removes only dirt.
- **With an empty hand, the material is air.** Press **Use held block** with an empty hand to
  carve. The material row then reads Air.
- **You can use the hotbar keys while the panel is open.** Press 1 to 9 to change the block in
  your hand, then press **Use held block**. A digit that you type into a text field goes into
  the field.
